implemented_requirements.evidence: config.py defines ROWS = 6 and COLUMNS = 7; Board.__init__ creates a grid of that size.
Game class stores a list of two Player objects, uses current_index and switch_player() to toggle turns in play_round().

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players choose columns by typing a number
implemented_requirements.evidence: Player.choose_column prompts with "choose a column (1‑{board.columns})" and reads input via input().
Game.play_round calls board.drop_disc() to place a disc and then board.render() to display the updated grid each turn.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line of four discs (win)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.check_win_from() checks four directions (horizontal, vertical, both diagonals) for a sequence of CONNECT (=4) matching discs; used after each drop.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect draw when the grid is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full() returns True when every cell is occupied; Game.play_round ends the round with announce_draw() when it becomes true.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Validate column choices (range and not full)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Player.choose_column uses board.is_valid_column() and board.is_column_full() to reject out‑of‑range or full columns.

implemented_requirements.requirement: End the game when a win or draw is detected
implemented_requirements.evidence: play_round() returns after a win (printing highlighted board) or after a draw; Game.run() exits the round loop accordingly.

judge.summary: The repository provides a complete, interactive Connect Four implementation. Configuration constants define the standard 7×6 board and a connect‑4 goal. Board, Player, and Game classes work together to handle disc placement, input validation, win/draw detection, and turn alternation. All core requirements are met with concrete code; no placeholder or stub logic is present. Minor stylistic concerns (e.g., redundant variable use in a print statement) do not affect functionality. The code appears ready to run as a console application.
